svg.title: ORION at a glance
svg.desc: ORION's architecture in one picture. On the left, the devices you meet him on: this machine's microphone, speakers and desktop; the HUD in a browser on a laptop, phone or tablet, which can carry his voice, share a screen or camera and lend its clipboard; other AI apps; Discord; and the HandTracking camera on a Raspberry Pi. In the centre, ORION, one Python process: the VoiceSession, the HUD server with its Surfaces, the IntentRunner, scheduled Jobs and the Watchers bring requests and announcements to the TurnRunner; the Brain prepares each turn with the Memory and calls on two things: the MCP hub, which every tool call goes through (it hides what this machine can't run, asks the Confirmer before a risky call after web content, marks tainted turns, traces every call and sizes pictures down), and the FallbackLLM, which thinks. On the right, the tools: in Orion's process, in his tools process, and external MCP servers. At the bottom, the storage in data/ (the Markdown memory, SQLite, skills, models, config.yaml) and the brains (your Claude plan through Claude Code, OpenRouter, Ollama).
svg.text: One Python process on your machine: your devices lend him a microphone, speakers and a screen, a language model thinks, and every tool call goes through the MCP hub.
The Runtime builds every part, applies settings live and runs the background loops.
